sections.h2: Where is Georgetown County and what makes it different?
sections.html:
Georgetown County runs from the Atlantic shore inland along several rivers, and about a fifth of its area is water. It covers 1,034.83 square miles, of which 813.61 are land and 221.22 are water, and the 2020 census counted 63,404 residents. The county seat is the city of Georgetown.

The largest community is Murrells Inlet. Other places include Pawleys Island, DeBordieu, Litchfield Beach, Plantersville, North Santee and Andrews, which is partly in Williamsburg County, and Garden City, mostly in Horry County. The coast along Waccamaw Neck is part of the Grand Strand, and Huntington Beach State Park protects part of the northern shore.

sections.h2: How do the rivers and coast affect a Georgetown County house?
sections.html:
Water is close to almost every parcel. The Great Pee Dee, Waccamaw, Black and Sampit rivers flow into Winyah Bay, the Santee River forms the southern boundary, and the Intracoastal Waterway crosses the county. The county also has Carolina bays, Sandy Island and the Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge.

The city of Georgetown sits at about 3 feet of elevation. Hurricane Hugo in September 1989 brought wind and storm surge along the rivers, and Hurricane Ian made landfall near Georgetown in September 2022. Annual rainfall at Georgetown County Airport averages about 55.43 inches, heaviest from June through September.

  • Ask for a flood zone and elevation record for the parcel before you list.
  • Gather roof, window and wind-damage repair records if you have them.
  • Check whether your stormwater fee is current, since it rides on the tax bill.

Having those answers ready helps when a buyer asks about storm history.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Georgetown County?
sections.html:
The city of Georgetown was incorporated in 1729, when Elisha Screven laid out a four-by-eight block grid, and it is the third oldest city in South Carolina. Indigo and rice built its colonial trade, and by 1840 the Georgetown District grew nearly half of the nation's rice crop. Timber and sawmills took over by 1900, and the port peaked as a lumber port around 1905.

The county is named for King George III, and the seat for him as Prince George. Georgetown District became Georgetown County in 1868. The Georgetown Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, keeps its original street names and lot numbers and includes more than fifty homes, public buildings and sites.

sections.h2: What drives the Georgetown County economy?
sections.html:
Accommodation and food service, health care and retail lead. Accommodation and food services provide 18.4 percent of jobs, health care and social assistance 15.4 percent, and retail trade 12.3 percent. The county's 2022 gross domestic product was about $3.3 billion.

Named employers include AGRU, Food Lion, International Paper, ScribeAmerica and Walmart. Georgetown is the second largest seaport in South Carolina, handling over 960,000 tons of material a year. The paper mill opened in 1936 under International Paper's Southern Kraft division, and Wikipedia reports that its closure was announced in October 2024, with 526 hourly and 148 salaried jobs lost. A steel mill opened in 1973 and closed in August 2015.

Wikipedia also notes that heritage tourism and retirement have grown in recent years.

sections.h2: When are Georgetown County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The state sets the window: taxes are payable from September 30 until January 15, and penalties start after that. A 3 percent penalty applies after January 15, an additional 7 percent after February 1 and an additional 5 percent after March 16, for 15 percent in all, under Section 12-45-180.

The county's own page for the Treasurer does not list due dates, so confirm the exact dates on your bill. The Treasurer sends notices, collects real and personal property tax and distributes the money to the county, municipalities, schools and special districts, but does not set amounts. The Assessor sets the value and the Auditor calculates the tax.

The Stormwater fee appears on the property tax bill and is due the same day. An incorrect stormwater bill can be appealed in writing to the director of Public Services within 30 days of the decision, with a map showing total area and impervious surface. Unpaid fees can result in liens.

sections.h2: How do you reach the Georgetown County tax offices?
sections.html:
County government is at 129 Screven Street, Georgetown, SC 29442, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 421270, Georgetown, SC 29442-4200. The county's main number is 843-545-3063.

The county's tax services page links separate pages for the Assessor, Auditor, Treasurer, Tax Collector, the Tax Sale and Forfeited Land Commission, and appeals. Offices keep property and owner records, and they rely on taxpayers to report address changes, so a seller who moved should update the Assessor and Auditor.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 Georgetown County reassessment change?
sections.html:
State law requires a countywide reassessment every five years, and Georgetown County's most recent one was the 2025 reassessment, with notices mailed September 15, 2025. Notices go only to properties whose value changed by at least $1,000, and a notice is not a tax bill. Bills arrive later in the fall.

Most long-held properties are capped at a 15 percent rise over the prior value, with exceptions for homes sold or transferred in the previous year, new construction or additions and newly added parcels. Capped properties show two values on the notice. State law also requires a millage rollback so the county does not collect extra revenue from reassessment. The county says that leaves little to no impact on taxpayers as a whole, though individual bills can move.

  • Primary residence: apply to the Assessor for the 4 percent rate.
  • Homestead exemption: owners 65 or older can apply to the Auditor for an exemption of up to $50,000 of value.
  • Buyers of rentals or commercial property can apply to the Auditor for the ATI exemption, which can reduce the increase in assessed value caused by a change of ownership by up to 25 percent.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Georgetown County value?
sections.html:
File a written objection within 90 days of the notice date. The notice includes an informal appeal form, and an Assessor's Office appraiser reviews it. No appraiser is required, there is no cost, and you can submit recent appraisals or sales data.

If you still disagree, ask for a hearing before the Board of Assessment Appeals. A further appeal goes to the South Carolina Administrative Law Court. Filing an appeal does not delay the tax bill, so pay on time to avoid penalties.

sections.h2: What happens at the Georgetown County tax sale?
sections.html:
The annual sale for 2026 is set for Monday, December 7, 2026, in County Council Chambers at 129 Screven Street. Bidders must register in advance, the fee is $25, and registration closes Friday, December 4, at noon. Bidding starts at 10:00 a.m., and winning bids must be paid in full by 5:00 p.m. that day.

Properties are advertised for three consecutive weeks in the Coastal Observer. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within 12 months. Interest is 3 percent in months one to three, 6 percent in months four to six, 9 percent in months seven to nine and 12 percent in the last three months, never above the forfeited land commission's bid. A tax deed is not a warranty deed, and the county tells buyers to talk to an attorney.

If a house you own may be on the list, ask the Delinquent Tax Department for the current amount owed.

faqs.q: When are Georgetown County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By January 15 under state law. A 3 percent penalty follows, then 7 percent more after February 1 and 5 percent more after March 16.

faqs.q: Does Georgetown County have a stormwater fee on the tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The stormwater fee is a line item on the property tax bill and is due the same day as the taxes.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Georgetown County property value?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date on the notice. File the form that comes with it, and the Assessor's Office reviews it for free.

faqs.q: When is the Georgetown County tax sale in 2026?
faqs.a: Monday, December 7, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. in County Council Chambers, 129 Screven Street. Registration closes December 4 at noon.

faqs.q: Does a Georgetown County reassessment mean my taxes go up?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The county rolls the millage back when values rise, so some bills go up, some fall, and the total collected stays about the same.
